A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ForesightKV research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning-benchmark evaluations, throughput measurements, reward and sampling ablations, and attention/token-error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds LongBench evaluations, sensitivity and length-transfer studies, and larger-model results.

M1.justification: v2 adds a task-specific inference adaptation: LongBench uses one compression after prefilling instead of repeated decoding-time eviction (Section 4.3). The scorer, Golden Eviction, ranking loss and GRPO remain unchanged. The sampling rewrite clarifies v1 Equation 2's negative-score rule and corrects the inconsistent description in Appendix B.2.

E1.justification: v2 adds LongBench's long-input tasks, covering document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks and code completion. Appendix E.4 also introduces science-domain training on SCP-116K followed by GPQA evaluation. These expand coverage beyond v1's retained training and evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain their baseline membership. H2O, SnapKV and R-KV remain, while RPC, DuoAttention and G-KV were already compared in v1 Appendix E.5. The additional studies reuse existing comparison methods and reward variants.

E3.justification: New protocols include non-thinking, single-compression LongBench evaluation at a 1K budget; controlled entropy thresholds; training-length comparison at 8K versus 32K; and Qwen3-14B task evaluation plus 14B/32B diagnostic settings. The original experiments' stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices E.4, E.5 and E.7 test entropy-threshold sensitivity, reward choice across domains and models, transfer from shorter training sequences, and larger-model attention-loss and entropy behavior. These substantially extend v1's retained reward, input-feature, sampling and token-error analyses.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 still reports mean pass@1 over 32 independent evaluations. The added experiments introduce no new seed disclosures, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Original matched results remain unchanged, but substantial new results appear. Table 7 reports LongBench averages of 38.95 for ForesightKV and 37.50 for SnapKV at 1K. Table 14 reports Qwen3-14B AIME2024 scores of 73.8 versus R-KV's 43.6 at 2K. Tables 10–12 and 15–16 add sensitivity, transfer and diagnostic findings.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains Proposition A.1 but adds a substantive derivation connecting maximum future-block scores to an upper bound on cumulative evicted attention mass. New local Lipschitz assumptions connect attention perturbations to logit and token-loss changes, replacing v1's direct assertion that the single-query bound validates Golden Eviction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: learned long-term KV importance, two-stage supervised/RL training, and stronger reasoning performance under reduced cache budgets. The additional evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains how restricted multinomial sampling balances ranking errors against irreversible noisy evictions, interprets the new threshold and transfer results, and extends applicability discussions to larger models. Appendix A also qualifies the theoretical connection as a surrogate argument with local stability assumptions.

D1.justification: The abstract adds code-access information. Appendix E.1 newly reports training costs for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B: approximately eight hours on two H800 GPUs for supervision and six hours on eight for RL. Appendix E.5 also explicitly identifies the main training maximum length as 32K.

R1.justification: v2 adds the LongBench citation, Bai et al. (2024). The related-work discussion, existing references and positioning around jointly using supervised and reinforcement learning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained. Local revisions expand the sampling explanation, reorganize Appendix A's argument, add experimental subsections and acknowledgments, and update publication and corresponding-author text.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially with dedicated LongBench, sensitivity, length-transfer and larger-model displays in Tables 7, 10–12 and 14–16. Existing tables are redistributed and renumbered. All four figure graphics are retained, with Figure 3 relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the retained method. Appendix A addresses the missing connection between the single-query bound and Golden Eviction's future-block surrogate, with explicit conditions for the loss argument. New long-input, larger-model, sensitivity and length-transfer experiments address important gaps in applicability and robustness evidence. Access and training-cost disclosures improve reproducibility. Uncertainty reporting remains limited, but the combined gains provide a clear overall improvement.
